item.title: The Daily Blogroll — Wednesday, 2 September 2026
item.description:
Tipa wrapped 31-for-31 Blaugust, reflected on Belghast and the IndieWeb, and said EverQuest Legends basically carried her posting month.

Azuriel sees Xbox’s disc-linked transferable digital license idea as the first real crack in the wall of digital game ownership.

Emily returns from a summer blogging break refreshed, with fanfiction, finished games, privacy worries, and a nostalgic GBA boss post queued up.

Owls closed out a 31-post Blaugust by reflecting on EQL, idea droughts, and keeping the blog personal instead of too meta.

Wilhelm highlights EverQuest’s new Lethar TLP server starting with The Serpent’s Spine, a very WoW-era guided leveling experiment turned nostalgia play.

Joar audits retirement like a business review and finds the real surprise wasn’t reading or fitness, but writing without planning for it.

Kelly added WordPress archive word counts with a PHP snippet, plus some honest notes on caching, SQL, and where the logic still wobbles.

Brennan argues open source needs to stop normalizing far-right politics, focusing this post on DHH, Shopify, Ruby Central, and Rails money.

Tim Bray fixed a Quamina data race, then used the detour to explain why he’s done accepting most LLM-generated PRs.

Scopique pitches a gloriously cursed wireless AI Ouija board powered by magnets, motors, a mic, and just enough engineering to spook the group chat.

Axxuy says work and exhaustion wrecked Blaugust plans, but the blog’s still alive and they’re hoping September goes better.

Tofutush argues AI “tells” in text and art mostly just misfire on real people, especially non-native and neurodivergent creators.

item.title: The Daily Blogroll — Tuesday, 1 September 2026
item.description:
Syp enjoys LOTRO’s bright Umbar palette, grabs an elk mount, and finds Octopath Traveler exactly the comfy JRPG mood he needed.

Tipa says EverQuest’s real endgame is epic quests, faction juggling, and race unlocks—not just Plane of Sky best-in-slot farming.

David’s Gunderholfen crew escapes Level 5 the hard way, fighting griffons and worgs just to limp back toward town.

Wilhelm wraps up Blaugust with 35 posts, a brief event history, and a very funny spam invite to join the Illuminati.

Tobold loves Star Wars Zero Company’s tactical combat and wildly flexible companion respecs, even if mission maps sound pretty fixed.

Andrew Plotkin releases The Witness source and scans, while weighing its 1938 atmosphere against its shallower mystery and dated Orientalism.

Anarchae posts a week 36 link roundup spanning anarchism, a Xerox bug, affordability, and Blaugust amid job-hunting exhaustion.

Magi vents through day one of quitting nicotine, swapping smoking rituals for patches, a zero-nicotine vape, and hopefully more writing.

JJM points to kernel.org’s AI crawler mess as a bleak internet arms race that burns CPU and makes hosting git repos feel pointless.

UltrViolet finishes 31-for-31 in Blaugust, then wonders whether shorter posts and helper tools fit better than forced daily writing.

Ghastly ends Blaugust on a high note, reflecting on 15 posts, community link-sharing, and a likely September blogging break.

Wakupan says Blaugust proved consistency boosts visibility and habits, while picking a clear topic makes blogging a lot more fun.

item.title: The Daily Blogroll — Monday, 31 August 2026
item.description:
Tipa is intrigued but skeptical about Wildmagic Frontier, especially how its HeroForge mini integration might blur cool feature and extra monetization.

Shintar is enjoying a lighter Star Wars: The Old Republic Galactic Season 11 grind, with Total Galactic War feeling refreshingly low-stress too.

Bhagpuss unpacks Neverness To Everness’s Fogden Game episode, enjoying the story turn while sorting through its shifting titles and narrative weirdness.

Joar gets candid about fitting World of Warcraft into marriage, kids, and work, and the quiet guilt gaming can carry in adult life.

Wes digs into re:Blue and ReXGlue, spotlighting Blue Dragon’s fan-made PC port while rounding up Donkey Kong 64 recompilation and MiSTer Third Strike news.

Wilhelm marks 20 years in EVE Online with an immersive capsuleer memoir on identity, immortality, and life in New Eden.

The Friendly Necromancer adds more comics, clearer sharing, and gem rewards to Poetry Slammers, even if each new circuit now sounds like a production marathon.

WCRobinson finds Metroid Prime 4: Beyond messy but compelling, with troubled development showing through alongside plenty of reasons for optimism.

Jeff Atwood reflects on Stack Overflow, Creative Commons, and how LLMs can absorb duplicate programming questions but not the human bonds behind the community.

Jeff revisits the pre-NTP days with the old Time and Daytime protocols, a neat bit of networking history with some very obvious limits.

Juhis wraps Blaugust with a Python A-to-Z recap, praising the structure while admitting the alphabet theme made cohesion a real challenge.

Cristian recaps Blaugust 2026 with hard-earned lessons on daily writing, blogging in your native language, and actually connecting with other bloggers.

item.title: The Daily Blogroll — Sunday, 30 August 2026
item.description:
Stargrace spots a Wurm Online rift in an absolutely awful mountainside location and keeps the verdict short: horrible.

Tipa shares how she’s using AI with EverQuest Legends logs, from vibe-coding a parser in Electron and TypeScript to ChatGPT-assisted build analysis.

Nimgimli argues it’s fine to drop games when sunk-cost guilt turns Steam-sale abundance and backlog management into homework.

Dávid rounds up Stargate-like games, especially Exogate Initiative’s base-management vibe and a charming unofficial Stargate point-and-click adventure.

Luna announces her giveaway winners and gives another cheerful shout for PancitoMerge and the story-rich delivery game Fading Serenades.

Welsh Troll says World of Tanks’ nonstop battle passes, mini-passes, events, and premium pressures have turned 16-year nostalgia into exhaustion.

Marc revisits Assault Suit Leynos, aka Target Earth, as an early Genesis standout that missed big sales but earned cult-classic longevity.

Wilhelm is glad Honest Game Trailers tackled Steam, from Half-Life 2-era digital distribution woes to sales, backlogs, Valve hardware, and early access.

Blockade85 gives Elite: Dangerous another real shot, finding slow progress through controls, docking, and Frame Shift frustration oddly rewarding.

Warner is deeply skeptical that Meta’s kid-safety settlement is anything more than a pricey PR move that still leaves Zuckerberg in control.

Jamie Zawinski is once again haunted by a mysteriously vanishing D key that only a Mac reboot or launching NoMachine seems to fix.

Dave Winer skips rude exit-popups, enjoys a beautiful Catskills day, and quietly pitches the nightly Scripting News email instead.

item.title: The Daily Blogroll — Saturday, 29 August 2026
item.description:
Frostilyte’s low-tier Pokémon Silver run heads toward Morty, detours through Sudowoodo and Togepi chores, and pauses to roast the Everstone.

Joel says Gris is a breathtaking watercolor platformer-puzzler, light on challenge but rich in atmosphere, music, and wordless emotional storytelling.

Margot talks backlog anxiety across Steam, Epic, PS5, and Switch, then highlights community projects that make actually playing those games feel doable.

Scopique breaks down Squadron 42’s delay to Q2 2027 and CIG’s attempts to steady Star Citizen after a rough 4.8 to 4.10 patch run.

Ellie revisits Marvel vs. Capcom as a slick, flashy 2D tag fighter that still lands, even if later sequels tend to steal its thunder.

Wilhelm and his daughter keep pushing Stardew Valley’s Community Center, upgrading the coop for a duck feather and making fishing easier with the cork bobber.

Michael rounds up a pile of obscure-game blog posts, celebrating everything from Gazillionaire to Journeyman Project 2 and inviting more people to join in.

Bruce Schneier’s weekly squid post spotlights Rhode Island’s very smelly ‘Squidpocalypse of ’26,’ featuring twenty tons of spilled squid.

Jimmy points readers to a new Analog Antiquarian post, a quick cross-link to his companion site’s latest historical essay.

Roger weighs IndieWeb ideals against the real cost and hassle of leaving Squarespace, framing self-hosting as possible but hardly painless.

Aywren compares blogging and YouTube, arguing video makes conversation easier while blogs still offer a more lasting home for thoughtful discussion.

Tipa wrestles with what it really means to belong to the IndieWeb, mixing practical membership steps with a candid, personal take on joining groups.
